name: Material Files
insteadOf: Files by Google / Mi File Manager / ad-supported file managers
hook: A clean, ad-free file manager with root access, archive handling, and network shares over FTP, SFTP, SMB, and WebDAV.
bullets: Material Design file browsing with dark theme and no ads anywhere
Root support for viewing and managing system files
Create, extract, and browse zip, tar, gz, and other common archives
Mount network storage: FTP, SFTP, SMB, and WebDAV servers
benefits: Does the file-manager job properly and then gets out of your way
Replaces three apps: local files, archive tool, and network client
Root and SAF access in one place for power users and tinkerers
Small, fast, and maintained — no bundled cleaners or 'boosters'
setupSteps: Install Material Files from F-Droid, Play Store, or GitHub releases
Open it and grant storage access when prompted
Add a network location from the side menu if you use FTP, SMB, or WebDAV
Enable root access in settings if your device is rooted
details: Material Files is an open-source file manager for Android 5.0 and up, built by Zhang Hai around one principle: clean Material Design, done properly. It covers the fundamentals with no ads and no junk — browse and manage local and SD-card storage, work with root access on rooted devices, and view, extract, and create common compressed formats (zip, tar, gz, and friends) without a separate archive app. Where it pulls ahead of the stock managers is network storage: it speaks FTP, SFTP, SMB, and WebDAV, so NAS shares and remote servers sit alongside local folders in one tree. It is GPL-3.0, roughly a few megabytes, available on F-Droid and GitHub releases, and deliberately contains none of the cleaners, boosters, or promotional cards that ship in the proprietary alternatives.
setup: App (Android) — grant storage access and browse
